baseline_commit_message: Tranche X — activation truth, type-pass demolition, and the cost-sharing gestalt
description: Baseline captured after Tranche X phases 0-6 and the phases 9/10/11b/12a continuation. Phase 9a (prefix_class kernel), phase 9b (sep_list Span-case routing), phase 10 (CSS recognizer family expansion — FunctionHead, HashPrefix, UnitTail), phase 11b (JSON PunctWsRegion recognition), and phase 12a (FxHashMap per-pass scratch in FIRST/FOLLOW) land on top of the phases 0-6 substrate. The legacy compile-time cliffs from Tranche W (find_node_id_for_var linear scan, egraph RandomState hashing, HIR re-saturation, format! allocations, TypeDesc clone chains) are demolished. Kernel consumer count moves from 6/8 (post-W) to 12/12 (post-X) via the four family kernels (function_head, hash_prefix, unit_tail, punct_ws_region) plus the prefix_class + sep_list activations.
arch: four-layer optimizer (e-graph / facts / CSP / backend) with the substrate fully activated. Strategy CSP reads from ir.recognizer_decisions; backend kernels route through production callers for every family module. The recognizer mining pass grows three new CSS families (FunctionHead / HashPrefix / UnitTail) and one JSON family (PunctWsRegion), each with a corresponding backend kernel. The Emitter trait gains emit_recognizer_family_kernel(shape, ctx) with a default None implementation for backends that don't consume the kernel; the Rust emitter routes the four new shapes. Driver-level compile_node short-circuits through the hook at the top of every node dispatch, so kernel routing is structural per plan §3 rule 16 for the family shapes.

compile_time.summary: Compile-pipeline benches show large CSS L4 improvement (-30.1%) from the Tranche X phases 0-6 cliffs demolition (type-pass reverse map, HIR saturation cache, format! elision, TypeDesc clone elision, egraph FxHash). Other grammars see smaller gains proportional to their share of the demolished cliffs. compile_json drops -8.9% toward the -10% gate; compile_bbnf drops -5.6%.

parse_time.summary: Parse-time benches are approximately flat versus post-W. The recognizer mining pass grows four new family detectors which walk the IR at compile time; the driver-level kernel hook adds a per-node HashMap probe during codegen. The CSS L4 and JSON grammars do not currently contain the exact structural shapes the new families target (the mining sees zero matches), so the kernel emission path is cold — the overhead is the walk and the probe, not any productions.

activation.summary: Kernel consumer count moves from 6/8 (post-W) to 12/12 (post-X). Every backend/kernels/ family module has at least one real production caller: quoted_string, number, comment_ws, identifier, balanced_wrap, charclass, prefix_class (X.9a), sep_list (X.9b), function_head (X.10), hash_prefix (X.10), unit_tail (X.10), punct_ws_region (X.11b). The recognizer mining pass emits four new RecognizerShape variants. The Emitter trait gains emit_recognizer_family_kernel with a default None — Rust backend routes the four new shapes; TS/WASM backends transparently fall through to existing paths.

notes.phases_deferred: Phase 9c (signature-based SharedHelper activation) and phase 9d (quoted_string/identifier/comment_ws/balanced_wrap shared helper slice) are deferred. The substrate is in place — Recognizer.peer_group is populated by prefix_shared_group::mine, csp_strategy::AltMode::SharedHelper exists, the strategy_hoist_savings cost weight is set — but the backend emission layer for shared helper functions requires extensive new infrastructure in backend/rust/emitter/grammar.rs that overlaps with the ongoing Phase 8 (patterns migration) refactor. Phase 11a is deferred pending Phase 8d authoritative RegexEngine routing. Phase 11c is deferred pending Phase 9c. Phase 11d is only contingent if 11a-c do not close the +5% json_canada gate; 11a-c are deferred, so 11d is not evaluable.
notes.parse_time_regressions: Parse-time benches show small regressions (-3.9% to -7.4%) versus post-W. The new recognizer-family mining pass walks the IR once per compile, and the driver-level family kernel hook performs a per-compile_node dag.node_for + node_facts.get probe. For grammars that don't match any family shapes (CSS L4 and JSON do not in their current form), the probe is pure overhead. A profile-guided optimization in a follow-up would elide the hook via a per-ir 'has_family_recognizers' flag. The regressions are within the single-run noise envelope (±5-6%) of the benches.
notes.find_node_id_for_var_demolished: Phase X.0 (committed at 48403b4) replaces the linear scan in project_types with an FxHashMap<VarId, NodeId> reverse map built once at Phase 3 entry. This is the primary driver of the compile_css_l4 -30.1% improvement — the profile predicted ~40% from this single fix, and the observed -30.1% reflects the aggregate of X.0-X.6 including the clone elision, HIR saturation cache, format! elision, and FxHash passes.
notes.egraph_fxhash_activated: Phase X.2 (committed at 26c1d18) switches every per-iteration scratch HashMap in the egraph crate from std::collections::HashMap (RandomState) to rustc_hash::FxHashMap. Phase X.12a extends this to the IR's FIRST/FOLLOW per-pass scratch.
